flows.title: The programme as run: co-brand fast-track and status matches
flows.story: 12% of members below 20 nights already hold Gold (credit-card fast-track, status match) and 94% above it do (sync lag). Eligibility at 20 nights instruments actual Gold, so the estimate is for guests whose status follows the threshold.

stages.question: What does the design look like before any effect is estimated?

metrics.help: First-stage jump in Gold attainment at the cutoff

stages.takeaway: Gold take-up jumps from 12% to 94%; the RDD compares the 16,549 members within ±5.0 nights of the cutoff.

stages.title: Density: is anyone gaming the threshold?
stages.question: Do guests pile up just above 20 nights?

metrics.help: fitted guests per night at the boundary

stages.takeaway: The density of qualifying nights is smooth through 20.

stages.title: Balance: are guests alike on either side?
stages.question: Do any pre-treatment covariates jump at the cutoff?
stages.takeaway: No pre-treatment characteristic changes at the threshold, so guests just below are a fair comparison group.

stages.title: Estimates: the jump at 20 nights
stages.question: How much does Gold move each outcome?
stages.takeaway: Gold raises room nights by +3.67 (95% CI 3.36 to 3.98); the true value is +3.40.

stages.title: Robustness: does the answer survive other choices?
stages.question: Is the estimate stable across bandwidths, placebo cutoffs and a donut hole?

metrics.label: Bandwidth sweep
metrics.help: room nights, h = 3 to 12, triangular, p = 1

metrics.label: Max deviation
metrics.help: largest gap to the headline estimate; pass if <= 3

stages.takeaway: The estimate holds across bandwidths, kernels and a donut hole, and false cutoffs show nothing.

stages.title: Economics: is Gold worth its perks?
stages.question: Per Gold member per year: incremental revenue against perk cost

metrics.label: Break-even margin
metrics.help: contribution margin at which perks exactly pay for themselves

stages.takeaway: Each Gold member returns $1,028 of extra revenue; after a 40% margin and $120 of perks the net is $291 (ROI +243%). Direct-booking gains are not monetised.

summary.reason: Valid design, a significant effect, and $291 net per member at a 40% margin.

flows.title: Strict night rule: Gold if and only if 20+ nights
flows.story: The same population under a clean rule with no fast-tracks. Take-up jumps from 0% to 100%, so sharp and fuzzy RDD should agree on the effect and the sharp one should be tighter.

stages.title: Replication: is this one draw typical?
stages.question: If we re-drew the placebo programme 30 times, how often would the design cry wolf?

metrics.label: Mean SE vs spread of estimates
metrics.help: equal when the standard errors are honest

stages.takeaway: Across 30 placebo draws the estimates centre on -0.020 and the interval excludes zero 3% of the time (nominal 5%): the method is unbiased, and one significant draw in twenty is expected.

stages.takeaway: Each Gold member returns $69 of extra revenue; after a 40% margin and $120 of perks the net is -$93 (ROI -77%). Direct-booking gains are not monetised.

summary.reason: The interval excludes zero (p = 0.033) but the true effect is 0. At the 5% level about 1 in 20 placebo programmes looks like this; over 30 re-draws the rate was 3%.

flows.title: Members top up stays to just reach 20 nights
flows.story: 40% of guests 1 to 3 nights short buy extra stays to land at 20 or 21 nights. The guests who reach Gold are no longer comparable to those who miss it, so the density test should fire and the estimate should not be trusted.
